key_insight: Within physics-informed learning, B-splines and neural networks can be directly compared as function representations, and the paper shows that splines can offer clearer convergence and optimization behavior on PDE problems with known solutions.
engineering_relevance: For PDE solvers, inverse design, and parametric modeling, the choice of representation affects training stability, sampling efficiency, and numerical precision requirements, not just final accuracy.
method: Set up a physics-informed learning framework using either neural networks or B-spline representations for PDE solutions.
Benchmark both representations on four closed-form test problems to compare accuracy, convergence, sampling needs, and loss minimization behavior.
Analyze asymptotic convergence rates and arithmetic precision sensitivity to isolate representation-driven effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical studies on four problems with closed-form solutions, evaluating accuracy, efficiency, convergence rates, sampling requirements, loss minimization, and required arithmetic precision.
watch_item: Results are based on benchmark problems with known solutions, so performance on noisy, high-dimensional, or strongly nonlinear real-world PDEs may differ.
paper_title: Comparison of neural and spline representations for physics-informed learning
